h.strategy: Borrow interaction patterns from other empirical sciences: epistasis in genetics (the effect of one mutation depends on genetic background, and beneficial mutations help fitter backgrounds less), diminishing returns in economics, and redundancy in engineered systems. Translate each pattern into a concrete conditional hypothesis about how an edit's effect varies with the parent configuration. Favor predictions that a practitioner thinking only mechanistically would get wrong, especially background-dependent sign changes and weaker gains in already-strong parents. Use conditions that many parents satisfy. In the flaw step, discard analogies that do not transfer and keep only those with a plausible general reason to hold.

hyps.why: Node 3 already receives deep conv features via edge 5, so another conv adds little and often displaces the valuable cell-level skip.
A sibling 3x3 conv summed into node 3 already supplies receptive field and capacity, so upgrading edge 4 saturates.
With edge 0 removed node 1 is zero, so changing edge 2 is nearly neutral instead of the usual penalty for replacing a useful op with pooling.
When edge 5 is none node 2 never reaches the output, so the normally harmful pooling edit on edge 2 has no effect.
A second identity into node 3 is redundant with the existing residual and replaces learnable capacity, compounding the many-skip penalty.
A duplicate identity-like input into node 3 adds no new function when edge 3 already provides the residual path.
Adding the residual where node 3 had no direct input is a large gain, while replacing an existing conv with skip is near-neutral or harmful.
Cutting edge 0 zeroes node 1 and silences the downstream 3x3 conv on edge 4, so the deletion is more damaging in that background.
With edge 5 absent node 2 is disconnected from the output, so the usually beneficial conv on edge 1 yields no gain.
When edge 4 is absent, removing edge 3 leaves node 3 dependent on a single path, a much larger loss than removing one of three inputs.
